title: Finite-index free lattice enlargement through a divisible subgroup
statement: Let $n\geq1$ be an integer, let $L$ be a free abelian group of finite rank (a finite free $\mathbf Z$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module]), let $B$ be an abelian group, let $D\subset B$ be a subgroup, and let $\varphi:L\to B$ be a group homomorphism. Suppose $D$ is $n$-divisible (for every $d\in D$ there is $e\in D$ with $ne=d$), $B/D$ is torsion-free (multiplication by every positive integer is injective), and $(B/D)/\operatorname{im}(L)$ is finite and killed by $n$. Then there exist a free abelian group $G$ of finite rank, an injective homomorphism $i:L\to G$ with $G/i(L)$ killed by a power of $n$, and a homomorphism $h:G\to B$ with $h\circ i=\varphi$, such that $G\to B/D$ is surjective. Free of finite rank means isomorphic to $\mathbf Z^d$ for some finite $d\geq0$.

proof.text: Put $C=B/D$, $p:B\to C$, $f=p\varphi$, and $S=f^{-1}(nC)\subset L$. The map $i:L\to S$, $x\mapsto nx$, is injective since $n\ne0$ and $L$ is torsion-free. The subgroup $S$ is finite free by [lem-weil-subgroup-finite-free-abelian-group-free]. Its inclusion in $L$ and the injection $i$ give opposite rank inequalities, so $S$ and $L$ have equal rank.

Apply [lem-sfb-full-rank-pid-smith-bases] to $S\subset L$, obtaining finite bases $e_j$ of $L$, $v_j$ of $S$ with $v_j=a_je_j$. Each $a_j$ is nonzero since $v_j$ is a basis vector. Put $t_j$ equal to the $j$th $S$-basis coordinate of $i(e_j)$. Comparing the $j$th $L$-basis coordinate gives $a_jt_j=n$. Consequently $i(e_j)=t_jv_j$.

As $v_j\in S$, choose $c_j\in C$ with $nc_j=f(v_j)$, and lift it to $z_j\in B$. The diagonal equation gives $a_j f(e_j)=n c_j=a_jt_jc_j$. Torsion-freeness of $C$ and $a_j\ne0$ imply $f(e_j)=t_jc_j$. Thus $u_j=t_jz_j-\varphi(e_j)$ lies in $D$. Choose $d_j\in D$ with $nd_j=u_j$ by the given divisibility. Set $b_j=z_j-a_jd_j$; then $t_jb_j=t_jz_j-nd_j=\varphi(e_j)$.

Define $h:S\to B$ by its basis values $h(v_j)=b_j$. On the basis of $L$, $h(i(e_j))=t_jb_j=\varphi(e_j)$, hence $hi=\varphi$. For every $y\in S$, $ny=i(y)$ (with $y$ viewed in $L$), so $S/i(L)$ is killed by $n$; take exponent $s=1$. Finally $h_Q$ says that $nc=f(x)$ for some $x\in L$, for each $c\in C$. Then $y=x$ belongs to $S$, and $nph(y)=ph(i(x))=f(x)=nc$. Torsion-freeness cancels $n$, proving $ph(y)=c$. Take $G=S$, in the same universe as $L$. This also covers $n=1$, zero rank, $D=B$ and noninjective $\varphi$; finiteness of the original cokernel is not needed.

proof_origin.place: Smith normal form proof replacing the cyclic induction in ILO XVI Lemma 3.6.4; the Lean statement is unchanged. Full-rank diagonal bases and n-divisibility construct G=S=f^{-1}(nC) and yield exponent one.

lean.statement: theorem divisible_unit_lattice_extension (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (L : Type u) [AddCommGroup L] [Module.Free ℤ L] [Module.Finite ℤ L] (B : Type v) [AddCommGroup B] (D : AddSubgroup B) (φ : L →+ B) (hD : ∀ d : D, ∃ e : D, n • e = d) [IsAddTorsionFree (B ⧸ D)] [Finite ((B ⧸ D) ⧸ ((QuotientAddGroup.mk' D).comp φ).range)] (hQ : ∀ q : (B ⧸ D) ⧸ ((QuotientAddGroup.mk' D).comp φ).range, n • q = 0) : ∃ (G : Type u) (_ : AddCommGroup G), Module.Free ℤ G ∧ Module.Finite ℤ G ∧ ∃ (i : L →+ G) (h : G →+ B), Function.Injective i ∧ (∃ s : ℕ, ∀ q : G ⧸ i.range, n ^ s • q = 0) ∧ h.comp i = φ ∧ Function.Surjective ((QuotientAddGroup.mk' D).comp h)
